title: Massive Response to Serial Hit-And-Run Driver
description:
Submit a tip! Tips@Midwest-Safety.com

Please consider JOINING for $1 a month. It *really* helps us do original reporting like this. 

CONTACT US:
Complaints? Video submissions? Sponsorships? Collabs? Business inquires? 
Email our board at Tips@Midwest-Safety.com

BE NICE:
The individuals presented in these videos may be suffering from the effects of alcohol, drug abuse, a mental health disorder or simply having a bad day. The videos should NOT be presumed to be representative of their general behavior. Everyone deserves to be treated with respect. 

RIGHT TO BE FORGOTTEN:
Midwest Safety practices the "Right to be Forgotten." If you were the suspect in a lower-level offense, you may email our board to request removal. 
Email: mn.safety.alerts@gmail.com

By the time as Rampage ended. age ended, 48-year-old Jeremiah Bailey injured three people and killed a fourth, 37-year-old U.S. Air Force Tech Sergeant Richard Padilla, stationed at nearby McDill Air Force Base. According to the police report, Bailey's second victim suffered a brain bleed, but survived. Detectives also discovered that during the hour between killing his third victim and hitting the fourth, Bailey drove to St. Petersburg where he struck another victim unloading groceries. A subsequent search of Bailey's vehicle yielded no firearm, and Bailey was found to be clenching a pack of cigarettes in his left hand. In all, seven officers fired at Bailey and confusion as to whether he was armed was likely due to the initial 911 call. As Bailey was running over his first victim, the victim's friend fired at Bailey, which can be heard on the 911 call. Two rounds were recovered from the vehicle matching the firearms that the officers were using, and one round was recovered that matched the friend's firearm. All officers were cleared of any wrongdoing, and the three officers who were injured, all by shrapnel or ricochets, were released and fully recovered. According to the police report, an interview with Bailey's girlfriend revealed that Bailey had suffered a traumatic brain injury after a three-story fall in the early 2000s and described seeing and hearing things that didn't exist, and that he often seemed confused or angry. He also recently was fired from his construction job and began drinking heavily. According to court records, Bailey was ordered to serve four years in Florida State prison for hitting a restaurant manager in the face with a beer bottle in 2019. And fighting with the officer who arrested him, Bailey had served his time and was on probation when he began his rampage throughout the Tampa Bay Area.

also discovered that during the hour between killing his third victim and hitting
the fourth, Bailey drove to St. Petersburg where he struck another victim unloading groceries.
A subsequent search of Bailey's vehicle yielded no firearm, and Bailey was found to be clenching
a pack of cigarettes in his left hand. In all, seven officers fired at Bailey and confusion
as to whether he was armed was likely due to the initial 911 call. As Bailey was running over
his first victim, the victim's friend fired at Bailey, which can be heard on the 911 call.
Two rounds were recovered from the vehicle matching the firearms that the officers were using,
and one round was recovered that matched the friend's firearm. All officers were cleared of any
wrongdoing, and the three officers who were injured, all by shrapnel or ricochets, were released
and fully recovered. According to the police report, an interview with Bailey's girlfriend
revealed that Bailey had suffered a traumatic brain injury after a three-story fall in the early
2000s and described seeing and hearing things that didn't exist, and that he often seemed
confused or angry. He also recently was fired from his construction job and began drinking
heavily. According to court records, Bailey was ordered to serve four years in Florida State
prison for hitting a restaurant manager in the face with a beer bottle in 2019. And fighting
with the officer who arrested him, Bailey had served his time and was on probation when he began
his rampage throughout the Tampa Bay Area.
